newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-NEW YEAR CHANGE DELAYS BRUSSELS BOURSE OPEN.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-NEW YEAR CHANGE DELAYS BRUSSELS BOURSE OPEN.

text.p: The Brussels stock market opened almost three hours late on Thursday after its trading system crashed due to the New Year date change.
"Trading has resumed as normal but opening hours will not be extended today," a Bourse official told Reuters.
Bourse trade resumed shortly before 1200 GMT compared with the normal 0900 GMT. The bourse closes daily at 1530 GMT.
The Bel-20 leading share index, which opened 0.14 percent lower, was down 0.39 percent to 1,888.08 at 1305 GMT.
Bourse director Olivier Lefebvre told Reuters the delayed opening was due to "a technical problem with the change of date which is causing problems in one programme."
Orders which were placed on December 30, the last trading day of 1996, were recognised instead by the bourse's computer as originating in December 1997.
This prevented investors and brokerages from changing their orders to reflect Wall Street's Tuesday plunge.
The Belgian market was closed on Tuesday and Wednesday for an extended New Year break.
The failure was the most serious technical problem to have hit the bourse since a new trading system was installed last year.
